made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/ropa-sheet-make.js, from ropa-set.html (window.ROPA.E) and the design of La ropa (the orchestrator's p7-spec, section ropa). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX = 120, OY = H / 2 + originY = 60. A box is the screen bounding box of its projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded half up to whole pixels (the things afloat at v -.5 and agua2 at u -.75 are exactly on a half pixel)
rules.uv: the set is laid out square to the picture: a spot is given in (u, v, z), u across the picture (to the right), v down it (towards the camera); plaza-base.js PZ.xy(u, v) = ((u + v) / R2, (v - u) / R2) gives the world x, y (world is that). On the picture sx = OX + u * S = 120 + 26 u, and sy = OY + (v / 2 - z * COS) * S = 60 + 13 v - 22.5 z. The beach: the water's edge at v 0, the wet strip to v 0.8, the horizon at v -3.5; the road from v 9.4; the line between the palms at v 2.7, z 1.75 (it sags up to .07 below that at its middle); the pegs at u -1.4, -0.72, -0.04, 0.64, 1.32; the picture holds u from -4.62 to 4.62
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the sand, the sea's shallows, the road; z 0.46: the bench's seat top) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). A small thing has a box (the spot's box): a piece on the line (cuerda1 to cuerda5, 16 x 16) hangs with its top row on sy and its middle on sx; the things afloat (14 x 9), the bag (14 x 10) and the shoes (24 x 8: two pairs of 12 x 8) have their bottom middle on the spot; the plate (16 x 10) has its bottom middle 8 px above it (on a small box); the driver (14 x 14) is centred on chofer. scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 41 rows drawn standing for a child; abuela standing mkAbuela (48 x 51): column 30, 51 rows drawn (engine.js); the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (row 25 of the canvas is on sy); abuela sitting mkAbuelaS (52 x 50): column 17 (her middle) and row 36 (her lap) on (sx, sy), the spot being the seat; a small thing: see spot. Whoever sits on the bench faces us: no sprite is turned (the makers draw them from the front)
rules.view: one window, wide, zoom 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture, x0 = its left edge (22 centres it). Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character. A piece on the line, a thing afloat, the plate, the shoes, the bag and the driver are upright planes like a character (the plate's plane is the plane through its spot: the same plane as the sand under it)

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the set's depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3): the guagua and its sign, the bench, the cabin, the palms' trunks and fronds hide whoever is behind them. The set's depth is the live depth after frame(0): the baked set with the palms' fronds at wind time 0 (window.DEPTH.live(); the fronds are not in window.DEPTH.z)
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where live[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (live: window.DEPTH.live() of the set page after frame(0)). The same rule as El calendario's sheet: the upright plane through the feet (a piece on the line is the plane through its top on the line's v)
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias; two planes within 0.001 are a tie and the later layer is drawn

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, 0, radius) at the world x, y of the spot, for a character standing on the ground (z 0). The spec gives no radius: these are the other places' (frog .45, grown-ups .35, children .28, the dog .3) (open point)
shadows.onSeat: whoever sits on the bench casts none (it is not ground: a shadow cast at the sand under them would show in front of them); the pieces on the line and the driver are in the air
